standard.title: Plan, create and publish texts
standard.description: plan, create, edit and publish imaginative, informative and persuasive written and multimodal texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students create and edit imaginative, informative and persuasive texts for familiar audiences using appropriate structure and language (AC9E2LY06). They have not yet focused on the full planning and editing cycle — including gathering ideas, selecting structure, using topic-specific vocabulary, and using digital tools and dictionaries.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish imaginative, informative and persuasive written and multimodal texts.

nodes.label: Planning and structuring
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a text by gathering information and selecting an appropriate structure for their writing purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan a text by gathering at least three ideas and selecting a text structure that suits the purpose, explaining why the structure was chosen.
nodes.typical_width: Gather information and ideas about a topic in preparation for writing; select appropriate text structure for the writing purpose and sequence content for clarity; use digital tools to plan, sequence and compose.
wider: Compare planning strategies for an imaginative text versus an informative text — discussing what is the same and what is different about each approach
Plan a multimodal text and discuss what additional decisions are needed compared with planning a written-only text
success_criteria: Student produces a plan (notes, web, list or draft structure) that gathers ideas before writing
Student selects a text structure appropriate to the purpose and can explain why

nodes.label: Creating with vocabulary and sentences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create texts using topic-specific vocabulary and appropriate simple and compound sentences to express and combine ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a text that includes at least two topic-specific vocabulary items and at least one compound sentence, explaining the purpose of each choice.
nodes.typical_width: Use appropriate simple and compound sentences to express and combine ideas; use vocabulary including topic-specific vocabulary relevant to the text type and purpose; select vocabulary deliberately to suit the topic.
wider: Compare vocabulary choices in a first draft with a revised draft and discuss how the vocabulary changes improved the text
Experiment with improving a generic sentence by replacing vague vocabulary with precise or topic-specific words, and evaluate the effect
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who have not created a text with deliberate vocabulary and sentence choices have no substantive draft to bring to N3 editing — N3 requires a composed text as its input.

response_modes.reason: Creating a text with deliberate vocabulary and sentence choices requires students to coordinate structural planning, grammatical knowledge (sentences, clauses) and vocabulary choice simultaneously. This is the composing integration that distinguishes planned, purposeful writing.

success_criteria: Student uses at least one topic-specific vocabulary item in their text
Student uses both simple and compound sentences — not only one type

nodes.label: Editing and publishing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can edit a text for spelling, apostrophe use and content quality, and publish using digital tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Edit a draft text by addressing at least one spelling or punctuation issue and one content improvement, explaining what was changed.
nodes.typical_width: Use print and online dictionaries and spellcheck to edit spelling, recognising that spellcheck doesn't catch all errors; check for correct apostrophe use for contractions and possession; use digital tools to publish texts.
wider: Compare a text before and after editing and evaluate whether the editing improved the text's clarity and accuracy
Develop personal editing strategies — a checklist approach — and apply it systematically to a draft

response_modes.reason: Editing is a skill that requires repeated practice — students improve through applying editing strategies across different texts and text types, not through additional conceptual instruction about what to check.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one substantive edit (not just a surface fix) to a draft
Student correctly applies apostrophes for contractions and/or possession after editing
